description: We are a student-led team passionate about space exploration, aerospace engineering, and innovation. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing LunaOps, an interactive prototype that compares lunar south-polar terrain using scientific data, visualizations, and decision-support tools. Our goal is to make lunar mission planning more accessible through research, creativity, and collaboration.
summary:
LunaOps: Lunar Mission Intelligence is an interactive lunar mission-planning decision-support prototype designed to help explore potential landing-site characteristics near the Moon's south pole. We developed a web-based platform that combines NASA lunar terrain data with interactive visualizations and a weighted decision-making system to compare two candidate sites.

LunaOps allows users to explore elevation and slope information, examine terrain characteristics side by side, and adjust mission priorities through a customizable decision model. It also incorporates Sun and Earth horizon intelligence using NASA/JPL Horizons resources to support further mission-planning exploration.

Our project addresses the challenge of evaluating complex lunar environments by making scientific data more accessible, understandable, and useful for preliminary comparisons. This is important because selecting potential lunar landing and exploration regions involves balancing multiple factors, including terrain conditions, illumination, communications, and operational constraints. LunaOps demonstrates how accessible data visualization and transparent decision-support tools can help inform future lunar exploration.
details:
LunaOps: Lunar Mission Intelligence, developed by Team Lunavelle, is an interactive platform designed to explore and compare potential landing-site characteristics near the Moon's south pole. Our goal was to make complex lunar terrain information easier to understand while demonstrating how scientific data can support preliminary mission planning.

The platform allows users to explore two candidate lunar sites through elevation and slope visualizations, side-by-side comparisons and an interactive Weighted Mission Site Decision Engine. Users can adjust mission priorities, experiment with different scenarios and examine how these changes influence site comparisons. We also integrated NASA/JPL Horizons information to explore Sun and Earth positions relative to the candidate locations, alongside downloadable PDF reports.

We developed LunaOps using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Python, with tools such as GitHub, GitHub Codespaces and Rasterio. Our project uses lunar terrain information from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), including LOLA elevation datasets, as well as NASA/JPL Horizons resources. No specialized physical hardware was required.

What makes LunaOps creative is its combination of scientific visualization and interactive decision-making. Rather than simply displaying lunar data, we wanted users to explore it, compare alternatives and understand how different mission priorities can influence planning decisions. Throughout development, we considered terrain characteristics, mission requirements, environmental conditions, data reliability and scientific limitations.

Ultimately, LunaOps is our attempt to bring space science, data analysis and interactive technology together to make lunar exploration more accessible and understandable. It is a preliminary decision-support prototype, not a landing-site safety certification system, and we hope it can inspire further exploration of the challenges involved in future lunar missions.
